page.layout: One page of text, with two coin illustrations at the top, centred above the text. Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: HERACLIVS, qui & Constantinus iunior, & nouus
Constantinus dictus est, Heraclii ex Fabia Eudoxia filius fuit:
admodū adolescens erat tum cum à patre imperiali diademate
donatus est.Hic verae pietatis cultor,cum nondum annum im-
perasset,Martinae nouercae insidiis,quae Heraclionae filio impe-
rium astrueret,veneno sublatus est. Vide Baptistam Egna. li. 2.
Pom.Læt.Succedit Heraclionas Heraclio anno mundi 4604.
à Christo nato 642.
HERACLION, siue Heraclionas,imperauit Constanti-
nopoli cum Martina matre,quæimperium inuaserat venefica:
hæc cum esset filia fratris Heraclii prioris Imperatoris,fuit item
illi Heraclio uxor,fuscepitque ex eo hunc Heraclionē siue He-
raclionam. Cum imperium male partum vix biennio tenuissent
mater,& filius decennis, in exilium à Senatu in Cappadociam
mittuntur:mulieri lingua praeciditur,ne oratione,qua plurimū
valebat,populos commoueret:puero nasus abscinditur,ne de-
cor aut gratia vultus in miseratione populum flecteret. Sena-
tus tunc sine militibus Imperatorem Constantem fecit, quod
raro contigit, vel ante vel post Tacitum. Pomponius Lætus,in
progenie Heraclii.

page.notes: Two coin illustrations at the top, not transcribed as text. Left coin: legend "IMP.HERACLIVS CONSTANTINVS" in a circle, with a bust facing right. Right coin: legend "MARTINA C E HERAC" with "AVG" at the left, showing two facing busts. The legends are engraved in the woodcut and read only partly. Some printed spellings are normalised per the rules, for example long s as s and the ligature "ft" as "st". The "Heraclionē" and "miseratione" marks are macrons read from a small scan; uncertain as to whether they are macron or tilde. Small stray marks in the margins (a pen-like scratch at left beside "à Christo", and specks at right) are not printed text and are omitted.
